title: The body and movement
subtitle: cheek, wrist, ankle; nod, shake hands, fold your arms
summary: Name the parts of the body and describe the small movements people make with them.

lesson.heading: Skin
lesson.text: The outer part of the body is covered in **skin**. It is the largest part of the body, and it needs care.

examples.text: Too much sun is bad for your **skin**.
She has very fair **skin**, so she burns easily.

lesson.heading: The head and the top of the body
rows: the part of your face above your eyes
the soft part of your face below your eye
the two soft parts around your mouth
the part of your face below your mouth
it joins your head to your body
the top of your arm, where it joins your body
the front of your body between your neck and your waist
the front upper part of the body

lesson.heading: Arms, legs and the middle
rows: the middle of your arm, where it bends
between your hand and your arm
the short thick finger at the side of your hand
the narrow part in the middle of your body
the side of your body just below your waist
the part of your body you sit on
the middle of your leg, where it bends
between your foot and your leg
one of the five at the end of your foot

lesson.heading: Breathing
lesson.text: People **breathe** through their nose or mouth. You **breathe in** and **out** about 12 to 15 times a minute, and much faster after exercise.

lesson.heading: Movements with your face
lesson.text: We **smile** when we are happy, and sometimes **smile at** people to be polite. We **laugh at** things which are funny. We sometimes **cry** if we are very unhappy or receive bad news, and we **yawn** when we are tired or bored.

examples.text: People **laugh at** things which are funny.
People sometimes **cry** if they're very unhappy.
People often **yawn** when they're tired, and sometimes when they're bored.

left.label: nod your head
left.text: Move it up and down. In many countries this means *yes*.
examples: She **nodded** her head and said nothing.
People **nod** their head when they mean 'yes'.

right.label: shake your head
right.text: Move it from side to side. In many countries this means *no*.
examples: He just **shook** his head and walked away.
People **shake** their head when they mean 'no'.

lesson.heading: Common expressions
rows: take their right hand in yours when you meet
move your hand to say hello or goodbye
make your hair tidy with a comb
clear your nose, usually when you have a cold
put one arm over the other in front of your chest

lesson.text: Be careful with the prepositions: you laugh at a joke, smile at a person, and wave to somebody.

exercises.prompt: Match the verb with the words that go with it.
The outer part of the body is covered in ___.
exercises.explanation: Too much sun is bad for your skin.

exercises.prompt: People often ___ when they're tired, and sometimes when they're bored.
exercises.explanation: We yawn when we are tired or bored.

exercises.prompt: People move their head up and down to mean 'yes'. They ___ their head.
exercises.explanation: Nod = move your head up and down. Shake = move it from side to side.

exercises.prompt: Why do people usually blow their nose?
exercises.explanation: You blow your nose when you have a cold.

exercises.prompt: Which part of the body is it?
The narrow part in the middle of your body, where your belt goes, is your ___.
exercises.explanation: Your waist is the narrow part in the middle of your body.

exercises.prompt: The part between your foot and your leg is your ___.
exercises.explanation: The ankle joins the foot to the leg; the heel is the back of the foot.

exercises.prompt: Which words are all parts of the face?
exercises.explanation: The cheek, the lips and the chin are all on your face.

exercises.statement: People usually cry when something is very funny.
exercises.explanation: People laugh at things which are funny. They cry when they are very unhappy or get bad news.

exercises.statement: You breathe in and out about 12 to 15 times a minute.
exercises.explanation: Correct. You breathe faster after running.

exercises.statement: You fold your arms when you want to say hello to a friend across the street.
exercises.explanation: You wave to somebody to say hello or goodbye. Folding your arms means putting one arm over the other.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence about meeting someone.
exercises.answer: I shook hands with her new boss.
exercises.explanation: We shake hands with someone, so the preposition is with.
